newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber closes higher on covering in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber closes higher on covering in slow trade.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market closed higher on covering and supply tightness but uncertainty in regional currencies movements and the summer holidays kept most buyers at the sidelines, dealers said.

"The players are confused over the market conditions," a dealer at a trading firm said. Some predicted that wet weather may start in Thailand soon while others were concerned over the Thailand's decision to default on taking delivery of rubber.
Lack of active consumer buying also limited the market's movements, dealers said.
There were scattered enquiries from local dealers while South Korea is tendering for SMR 10 and 20 rubber, they said.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 295 cents, SMR L at 275, SMR 5 at 254, SMR 10 at 249, SMR 20 at 247 and latex at 191.
At the close, August RSS1 buyer ended two cents up at 247.50 cents (94 U.S. cents) a kg and August SMR 20 buyer was up 1.50 cents at 246.
Some traders said there was a slight tightness in supply because of the weather conditions in producing countries.
